subject.title: Codex app-server: keyed turn routing, client-scoped rate limits, and resume subscription safety

question: Should maintainers sponsor a bounded current-main implementation of the surviving Codex app-server routing, rate-limit, and resume-safety pieces now, or split/defer this runtime refactor?
rationale: The issue is source-backed and aligned with current priorities, but it carries protected maintainer routing and touches Codex auth/session state, shared clients, and upstream app-server subscription semantics.

options.title: Sponsor bounded implementation
options.body: Re-implement only the router, client-scoped rate-limit cache, per-client runtime handlers, resume-safety split, and client-factory cleanup on current main with focused upgrade and concurrency tests.

options.title: Split into smaller bugs
options.body: Track rate-limit cache scoping, turn routing, and resume subscription safety as separate issues if maintainers want narrower review and validation slices.

options.title: Defer pending live repro
options.body: Keep this as maintainer backlog until a live multi-client Codex app-server reproduction is available, accepting the current source-level risk in the meantime.

recommendation.title: Sponsor bounded implementation
recommendation.body: Re-implement only the router, client-scoped rate-limit cache, per-client runtime handlers, resume-safety split, and client-factory cleanup on current main with focused upgrade and concurrency tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the current issue and related refactor context and recently merged the binding-store work that any bounded implementation must preserve.
